name: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023
description: India's main criminal code — defines crimes (theft, assault, fraud, cheating, offences against women, murder, etc.) and their punishments. Replaces the old Indian Penal Code (IPC).

name: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023
description: Criminal procedure — how police investigate, arrest, file FIRs, and how criminal trials proceed. Replaces the old Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).

name: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023
description: India's law of evidence — what counts as valid evidence in court (witnesses, documents, digital evidence, confessions). Replaces the old Indian Evidence Act.

name: The Constitution of India
description: The supreme law of India — fundamental rights, duties, structure of government, and how the state must treat citizens.

name: Indian Contract Act, 1872
description: Governs agreements and contracts — what makes an agreement legally valid, breach of contract, compensation, and related remedies.

name: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
description: Rights of consumers — defective goods, deficient services, unfair trade practices, e-commerce complaints, and how to approach consumer courts/commissions.

name: Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023
description: How personal data must be collected, used, and protected by companies/apps/websites in India, and what rights individuals have over their own data.

name: Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005
description: How any citizen can request information from government bodies, timelines for response, and the appeals process if refused.

name: The Companies Act, 2013
description: Governs how companies in India are formed, run, and regulated — director duties, shareholder rights, company disputes, fraud, and winding up.

name: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
description: Marriage, divorce, judicial separation, maintenance, and custody rules for Hindus (also applies to Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs).

name: The Special Marriage Act, 1954
description: Civil marriage law allowing any two people in India to marry regardless of religion, plus related divorce and maintenance provisions.

name: Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939
description: Grounds on which a Muslim woman can obtain a decree dissolving her marriage through the courts.

name: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
description: Criminalises instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) and provides for subsistence allowance and custody rights for the wife.

name: The Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937
description: Establishes that Muslim Personal Law (Shariat), not custom, governs marriage, inheritance, and family matters for Muslims in India.

name: Compendium of Important Supreme Court Judgments
description: A reference collection of landmark Supreme Court cases and what each one decided, organised by legal topic — use this to find real case citations.
